iteration_note: Each exam is administered annually; 10 recorded editions. Edition 1 (2017) is the canonical paper below; editions 2-10 are tracked in the version ledger as they are authored.

agents.I: State the First Isomorphism Theorem for groups and rings, and state when a module is free.
agents.II: Prove that every finite integral domain is a field.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Lang, Algebra — Graduate Texts in Mathematics 211.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline sheaf-theory questions (field 2). Trap: must not claim every module is free without an 'over a field or PID' qualification.

agents.I: Define a variety and a scheme; distinguish affine from projective objects.
agents.II: Show that the affine coordinate ring of A^n is a UFD and compute the ideal of a k-point.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hartshorne, Algebraic Geometry (1977).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline pure commutative-algebra questions (field 1). Trap: must not equate smooth with nonsingular without the correct hypotheses.

agents.I: State Fermat's little theorem and Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions.
agents.II: Prove Fermat's little theorem via the multiplicative group of Z/pZ and derive the Euler phi generalization.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hardy & Wright, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline cryptographic-implementation questions (field 55). Trap: must not claim the Riemann Hypothesis is proved.

agents.I: State Urysohn's lemma and the definition of compactness.
agents.II: Prove that a continuous bijection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Munkres, Topology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline metric-space analysis (field 8). Trap: must not claim every continuous bijection is a homeomorphism.

agents.I: Define a smooth manifold, tangent space, and curvature; state Gauss-Bonnet.
agents.II: Derive the Gauss curvature of the unit sphere from the first fundamental form.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline general-relativity physics (field 204). Trap: must not claim every connection is Levi-Civita.

agents.I: State the correspondence between Lie algebras and simply connected Lie groups, and the notion of a highest-weight module.
agents.II: Show that sl(2) is simple and construct its finite-dimensional irreducible representations.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Humphreys, Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline algebraic-group theory (field 2). Trap: must not assume every Lie algebra is semisimple.

agents.I: State the Hahn-Banach and Banach-Steinhaus theorems.
agents.II: Prove the closed graph theorem using the Baire category theorem.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Rudin, Functional Analysis.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline measure-theory questions (field 8). Trap: must not claim every Banach space is a Hilbert space.

agents.I: State the dominated convergence theorem and Cauchy's integral theorem.
agents.II: Prove the Cauchy integral formula and deduce Liouville's theorem.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Rudin, Real and Complex Analysis.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline harmonic analysis (field 9). Trap: must not conflate Riemann and Lebesgue integrability.

agents.I: State Plancherel's theorem and Fourier inversion on Schwartz space.
agents.II: Prove Plancherel's theorem for L^2(R) starting from Fourier inversion on the Schwartz class.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Stein & Weiss, Introduction to Fourier Analysis on Euclidean Spaces.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline DSP engineering (field 487). Trap: must not claim unconditional pointwise Fourier convergence.

agents.I: Classify linear second-order PDEs and state Hadamard well-posedness.
agents.II: Solve the Cauchy problem for the heat equation and prove the smoothing property.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Evans, Partial Differential Equations.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline numerical schemes (field 26). Trap: must not claim every PDE has smooth solutions.

agents.I: Define a Lyapunov function and state the Poincare-Bendixson theorem.
agents.II: Prove the Poincare-Bendixson theorem for planar systems, or show a rotation of the circle is ergodic iff irrational.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Strogatz, Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline control-design (field 125). Trap: must not equate chaos with randomness.

agents.I: State Birkhoff's pointwise ergodic theorem and the definition of ergodicity.
agents.II: Show that an irrational rotation of the circle is ergodic with respect to Lebesgue measure.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Walters, An Introduction to Ergodic Theory.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline stochastic-process statistics (field 41). Trap: must not claim a.e. convergence implies L1 convergence without integrability.

agents.I: Define a C*-algebra and state the Gelfand-Naimark theorem; distinguish von Neumann algebras.
agents.II: Prove the commutative Gelfand-Naimark theorem (isometric isomorphism with C(K)).
agents.III: Situate the theory: Murphy, C*-Algebras and Operator Theory.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline plain functional analysis (field 7). Trap: must not claim every C*-algebra is commutative.

agents.I: State the Yoneda lemma and the definition of an adjunction.
agents.II: Prove the Yoneda lemma and derive that the Yoneda embedding is fully faithful.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Mac Lane, Categories for the Working Mathematician.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline set-theoretic foundations (field 18). Trap: must not conflate equivalence with isomorphism.

agents.I: Define Ext and Tor and state the long exact sequence from a short exact sequence.
agents.II: Derive the long exact sequence in homology from a short exact sequence of chain complexes.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline category theory (field 14). Trap: must not compute nontrivial Tor over a field.

agents.I: State the inclusion-exclusion principle and Ramsey's theorem.
agents.II: Prove inclusion-exclusion and use it to count derangements.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Stanley, Enumerative Combinatorics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline graph-algorithmic complexity (field 51). Trap: must not present a probabilistic-method argument without the Lovasz local lemma.

agents.I: State Hall's marriage theorem and the definition of a perfect matching.
agents.II: Prove Hall's marriage theorem via max-flow min-cut.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Diestel, Graph Theory.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline algorithmic complexity for graphs (field 51). Trap: must not claim the four-color theorem is hand-provable.

agents.I: State the role of the ZFC axioms and the independence of the continuum hypothesis.
agents.II: Outline the forcing argument that CH is independent of ZFC.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Kunen, Set Theory.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline model theory (field 19). Trap: must not claim CH is provable or disprovable.

agents.I: State the compactness and Lowenheim-Skolem theorems.
agents.II: Prove the compactness theorem via ultraproducts.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Marker, Model Theory: An Introduction.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline forcing (field 18). Trap: must not claim compactness yields standard models of the negation of PA.

agents.I: State Godel's incompleteness theorems and the notion of a recursive axiomatization.
agents.II: Sketch the proof of Godel's first incompleteness theorem for PA, including arithmetization.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Enderton, A Mathematical Introduction to Logic.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline computability-theory algorithms (field 54). Trap: must not claim Godel showed mathematics is inconsistent.

agents.I: State the difference between condition number and algorithmic stability.
agents.II: Derive the truncation error of the trapezoidal rule and its order of convergence.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Trefethen & Bau, Numerical Linear Algebra.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline existence proofs (field 10). Trap: must not blame roundoff alone; discretization error counts.

agents.I: State the KKT conditions and when they are necessary and sufficient.
agents.II: Derive the KKT conditions for a convex program with inequality constraints.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Boyd & Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline deep-learning optimizers (field 90). Trap: must not claim a nonconvex local minimum is global.

agents.I: Derive the Euler-Lagrange equation and define weak vs strong minima.
agents.II: Derive the Euler-Lagrange equation from a first variation and solve a free-endpoint problem.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Gelfand & Fomin, Calculus of Variations.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline optimal-control theorems (field 126). Trap: must not ignore natural boundary conditions.

agents.I: Derive the wave and heat equations from conservation laws.
agents.II: Derive the wave equation for a vibrating string from Hooke's law.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Courant & Hilbert, Methods of Mathematical Physics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline QFT formalism (field 197). Trap: must not let physical intuition replace well-posedness checks.

agents.I: Set up and nondimensionalize a model, identifying its regimes.
agents.II: Nondimensionalize the diffusion equation and identify the dominant regime from the dimensionless groups.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Logan, Applied Partial Differential Equations.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline proof-level PDE theory (field 10). Trap: must not apply a model outside its derivation regime.

agents.I: State the CFL condition and distinguish upwind from central schemes.
agents.II: Prove the CFL condition for a 1D advection scheme and state the stability constraint.
agents.III: Situate the theory: LeVeque, Finite Volume Methods for Hyperbolic Problems.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline turbulence-theory derivations (field 213). Trap: must not claim stability implies accuracy (numerical diffusion).

agents.I: State Hadamard ill-posedness and Tikhonov regularization.
agents.II: Show that numerical differentiation is ill-posed and derive the Tikhonov regularized solution.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Kaipio & Somersalo, Statistical and Computational Inverse Problems.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical imaging (field 327). Trap: must not claim regularization removes noise without bias.

agents.I: State the Weierstrass theorem and best approximation in L2 vs Linf.
agents.II: Prove the Weierstrass approximation theorem using Bernstein polynomials.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Trefethen, Approximation Theory and Approximation Practice.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline quadrature rules (field 21). Trap: must not ignore the Runge phenomenon.

agents.I: Distinguish regular from singular perturbations and define matched asymptotic expansions.
agents.II: Compute the leading-order asymptotic of an integral via Laplace's method.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Bender & Orszag, Advanced Mathematical Methods for Scientists and Engineers.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline numerical solvers (field 21). Trap: must not call a divergent asymptotic series wrong.

agents.I: State the Fredholm alternative for compact operators.
agents.II: Prove the Fredholm alternative for a compact integral operator on L2.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Kress, Linear Integral Equations.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline group harmonic analysis (field 9). Trap: must not claim Volterra equations always close in closed form.

agents.I: Set up the SIR model and define the basic reproduction number R0.
agents.II: Derive R0 for the SIR model and prove the threshold theorem for outbreak.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Murray, Mathematical Biology.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline molecular-biology mechanisms (field 263). Trap: must not claim R0 > 1 guarantees an outbreak.

agents.I: Reduce a real engineering problem to a solvable mathematical model with explicit assumptions.
agents.II: Set up and solve the heat balance of a cooling fin with boundary conditions.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Howison, Practical Applied Mathematics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline discipline-specific engineering design (fields 474-491). Trap: must not ship a model without validating assumptions.

agents.I: State the Rao-Blackwell theorem and the notion of sufficiency.
agents.II: Prove the Rao-Blackwell theorem and verify sufficiency for a canonical family.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Lehmann & Casella, Theory of Point Estimation.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline Bayesian inference (field 34). Trap: must not claim unbiasedness alone makes an estimator best.

agents.I: State Bayes' rule in full and the role of a conjugate prior.
agents.II: Derive the posterior for a normal-normal conjugate model and write it in shrinkage form.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline frequentist testing (field 33). Trap: must not claim any prior is truly uninformative.

agents.I: State the bias-variance trade-off in high dimensions and LASSO sparsity.
agents.II: Prove the bias-variance decomposition and derive the LASSO subgradient conditions.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hastie, Tibshirani, Wainwright, Statistical Learning with Sparsity.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline solver optimization (field 90). Trap: must not claim support recovery without irrepresentable conditions.

agents.I: State stationarity and the roles of ACF and PACF in ARIMA identification.
agents.II: Derive the ACF of an AR(1) process and the Yule-Walker equations.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Box, Jenkins, Reinsel, Time Series Analysis.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline deep-learning forecasting (field 84). Trap: must not claim unit-root tests are decisive.

agents.I: Define the hazard function and state the Cox proportional hazards assumption.
agents.II: Derive the partial likelihood for the Cox proportional hazards model.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Kalbfleisch & Prentice, The Statistical Analysis of Failure Time Data.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline trial design (field 331). Trap: must not ignore censoring.

agents.I: State kernel density estimation bias-variance and the notion of a rank test.
agents.II: Compute the MSE of a kernel density estimator and derive the optimal bandwidth order.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Wasserman, All of Nonparametric Statistics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline parametric inference (field 33). Trap: must not claim the bootstrap fixes small-sample bias.

agents.I: State randomization, blocking, and factorial designs; explain confounding control.
agents.II: Construct a 2^k factorial design and compute main-effect and interaction estimates.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Box, Hunter, Hunter, Statistics for Experimenters.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline regulatory trial design (field 331). Trap: must not claim every factorial cell needs replication.

agents.I: State VC dimension and uniform convergence of empirical risk.
agents.II: Sketch the VC generalization bound via the Sauer-Shelah lemma.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Shalev-Shwartz & Ben-David, Understanding Machine Learning.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline ML engineering (field 63). Trap: must not claim PAC bounds are tight in practice.

agents.I: Define the Markov property and state martingale convergence theorems.
agents.II: Prove the optional stopping theorem for bounded martingales.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline finance applications (field 390). Trap: must not claim unconditional martingale convergence.

agents.I: State the central limit theorem and its conditions.
agents.II: Prove the CLT via characteristic functions using Levy's continuity theorem.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Feller, An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications, vol. 2.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline measure theory (field 8). Trap: must not apply the CLT to heavy tails without normalization.

agents.I: State variance-reduction techniques and MCMC convergence diagnostics.
agents.II: Prove the variance reduction of importance sampling and derive the optimal proposal.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Robert & Casella, Monte Carlo Statistical Methods.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline quadrature theory (field 21). Trap: must not treat MCMC samples as i.i.d.

agents.I: State kriging and the variogram; define spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I).
agents.II: Derive the kriging equations from best linear unbiased prediction.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Cressie, Statistics for Spatial Data.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline geospatial software (field 100). Trap: must not claim kriging is unbiased with a misspecified covariance.

agents.I: State Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and when it beats random-walk; define burn-in.
agents.II: Prove detailed balance for Metropolis-Hastings and derive the acceptance ratio.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Brooks et al., Handbook of Markov Chain Monte Carlo.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline convergence proofs (field 43). Trap: must not confuse effective sample size with sample count.
